kept.excerpt: Seventeen candidates — 12 Republicans, two Democrats, and three independents — are running in the open top-four primary for governor of Alaska. Tom Begich, Click Bishop, David Bronson, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, Bill Walker, and Bernadette Wilson lead in polling and media attention.
kept.relevance: Identifies Bishop among six leading contenders competing for four advancement slots immediately before the primary.

kept.excerpt: Crowded fields of candidates for governor, U.S. House and the state Legislature will compete for spots on the general election ballot. Republican gubernatorial candidates include former state senators Click Bishop, Shelley Hughes and Lesil McGuire, former Anchorage Mayor Dave Bronson, former state revenue Commissioner Adam Crum, former state Attorney General Treg Taylor and conservative activist Bernadette Wilson.
kept.relevance: Provides a final pre-election preview documenting the depth of Bishop’s Republican competition.

kept.excerpt: Alaska’s two leading Democratic candidates for governor have quietly been discussing whether one of them should quit the race if both are among the top four vote-getters in Tuesday’s primary election. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins and Tom Begich each said by phone on Thursday that they have been discussing different scenarios about what could happen when the final votes are counted. Under Alaska’s election system, the top four vote-getters, regardless of political party, advance to the November general election.
kept.publisher: Alaska Public Media / Alaska Beacon, James Brooks
kept.relevance: Documents pre-election strategic withdrawal discussions relevant to how the eventual general-election field could be formed.

kept.excerpt: More than 31,000 Alaskans have already cast their ballots ahead of the statewide primary. Polls open at 7 a.m., and the top four vote-getters, regardless of party, advance to November. Mail ballots must be postmarked by election day.
kept.relevance: Confirms that voting was underway and supplies the primary’s operating rules and timing without reporting results.

kept.excerpt: Seventeen candidates are running to be Alaska’s next governor, and early voting is underway for the Aug. 18 nonpartisan, pick-one primary, which will narrow the field to four. Alaska Public Media reached out to every campaign that raised $50,000 or more as of the mid-July fundraising reporting deadline. Republican candidate Click Bishop served 12 years in the Legislature after serving as labor commissioner under Governors Sarah Palin and Sean Parnell.
kept.publisher: KMXT / Alaska Public Media, Eric Stone
kept.relevance: Offers a recent Bishop interview and establishes his experience and inclusion among campaigns meeting the broadcaster’s fundraising threshold.

kept.excerpt: Republican candidate for governor Click Bishop and his independent running mate, Greta Schuerch, visited Kotzebue last week as part of a statewide tour ahead of the August 18 primary. Bishop is a former state senator from Fairbanks.
kept.relevance: Confirms an active statewide campaign and outreach to rural Alaska shortly before the primary.

kept.excerpt: Four union officials are helping to lead a newly formed political group supporting Republican Click Bishop, a former state senator from Fairbanks with a long background in the labor movement. The group will have a six-figure budget to spend on Bishop and running mate Greta Schuerch ahead of the mid-August primary, according to Alaska AFL-CIO president Joelle Hall. The AFL-CIO itself has not issued a formal endorsement in the race.
kept.publisher: Alaska Beacon / Northern Journal–Anchorage Press, Nathaniel Herz
kept.relevance: Documents an organized funding and mobilization resource that could help Bishop distinguish himself in the crowded primary.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-08-19. Included only sources with explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff; all selected items are pre-election reporting. Excluded primary-results reporting even when dated August 18–19, later developments, prediction-market or betting material, and undated or subsequently updated election and polling pages. No forecast or outcome is supplied. Dates and excerpts were checked against web_search-indexed source text.
